rationale: fastdiff_flow_pixel_unconstrained-claude-agentic: train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, noise_i0=100000.0, noise_sigma_e=10.0, fd_recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/fast_diffusion_pixel_unconstrained.pt, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.7, fd_recon_eta=1.0, fd_recon_dc=1, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=5, fd_recon_dc_relax=0.9, rationale=iter-2: DC-anchor probe, fd_recon_dc_relax 0.5->0.9 (near-hard CG projection onto the measured 128-view sinogram). PRIOR (iter-1): hr=0, val_rmse 0.01428 vs sparse-FBP baseline_rmse 0.00521 (recon 2.7x WORSE than FBP), SSIM 0.741 vs 0.920, PSNR 27.58 vs 36.32 dB. FAILURE MODE: the out-of-domain Mayo-trained pixel prior (out_scale 0.05, breast mu up to 0.5) drags the iterate far off the data solution; DC blend at 0.5 is too weak to hold it. ONE KNOB: dc_relax 0.5->0.9 pulls the recon much harder toward the data (FBP-consistent) solution where PSNR/RMSE live. HYPOTHESIS: if I raise dc_relax to 0.9 the recon collapses back toward the FBP baseline and RMSE drops sharply, testing whether the deficit is a weak-DC/prior-drift problem (recoverable) vs a fundamental prior-domain mismatch. eta/steps/init_t held from iter-1. Budget: same sampler cost ~185s, well inside 20 min.
